Subject: Initial screener: residency + retention for hosted API

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Novus is moving quickly on a proof-of-concept and our security team has a short screener to confirm data flows for hosted APIs. Could you confirm the following at a high level so I can pass them to our legal/compliance team?

1) Where customer request/response data is stored by default (region(s))
2) Retention window for request logs and generated content for hosted customers
3) Whether we can request full deletion of a tenant and associated artifacts (timeline)
4) Whether Redwood stores any long-lived backups that include customer content

If you prefer, we can accept a short PDF or a pointer to your RFI doc. Appreciate a reply by EOD Pacific if possible — our procurement timeline is tight.

Hi Jane — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a concise PDF that covers the items and includes an ops contact for a deeper review.

1) Regions: Hosted API customer content is stored in the region selected at account creation. By default we store data in AWS regions mapped to the customer region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). We also offer explicit region pinning for enterprise customers.

2) Retention: Customer request/response payloads are retained for 30 days by default to support analytics and abuse protection. Request metadata (timestamps, IP anonymized) is retained for 90 days. Logs required for billing and SLO analysis are retained for 365 days. These windows are configurable under contract for Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Deletion: We support tenant-level erasure requests. Typical timeline: initiate export & confirmation (1–3 business days), backend purge (up to 7 business days), final verification & audit record (additional 2 business days). For standard hosted accounts we provide a documented erase workflow; for enterprise we offer a short SLA to accelerate timelines.

4) Backups: We do not retain long-lived backups containing plaintext customer content beyond our standard disaster-recovery retention window. Short-term snapshots (encrypted at rest) exist for 14 days strictly for recovery; they are rotated and not accessible for analytics. We can include a certificate of destruction for contractual commitments.

Jane — good questions, answered inline and updated in the attached PDF (v1.1).

• Region locality: All customer metadata and request/response content is served and stored in the selected region by default. In rare fallback scenarios (outage or capacity constraints) routing may send requests to a compatible nearby region; we log any cross-region routing events and surface them to customers. Customers can opt into strict region-locking for higher tiers.

• Generated outputs: Yes — generated model responses are treated the same as request payloads for retention and deletion purposes (default 30 days). Any cached prefixes used for performance (prefix/KV cache) follow the same retention and are subject to erasure on tenant deletion.

• Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for customer data and snapshots. Keys are customer-segregated for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers use our KMS with customer-specific key rotation controls available via contract.

I've attached the updated PDF and included a single-paragraph summary for your legal team. If Novus needs a signed addendum for region-lock or retention shortening, Ben (cc) can pick up procurement/contract language.
